ctx.x: Shad Shell -- Shelton Hemphill was from Birmingham, Alabama, out of a high school that turned out quite a few great musicians from a great band leader down there -- we called him Fess Watney, and Shelton Hemphill graduated from that school, and he was an excellent reader. He had big shoulders like Cootie Williams, Woodchop, you know, and when he would play, he would sit down, he would actually pump. He was the first trumpet player in anybody's band, and he was in my Wilberforce Collegians band, one of the…

And he was in that group that we played the battle of music with the McKinney's Cotton Pickers Kenny Scott in Detroit, and we also went to New York at the Savoy, and so forth, ballroom, The Home of The Happy Feet, down there on 143rd and Lenox Avenue. And Shelton was great, and the band that we played against there was the great Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, and getting back to saying a little bit about Shelton, Shelton was an excellent reader. He was what you call a sight reader. And he wanted to continue in…

And he was with a band before that, that Lucky Millinder and Mills Rhythm Blue A Band, he was also in that band. And there were quite a few name bands that Shelton had played in after the Collegiates, but I think his greatest triumph was when he was with Duke because he always wanted to get with the great Duke Ellington. He always also talked Duke when he was with the Collegiates. And he made it, and I just read recently in the DownBeat where he passed, so I was real touched on that because I knew him just like a…
